ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the line $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+8$ intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. A moving point C starts from point B and moves at a uniform speed of 1 unit per second in the direction of $BA$. Simultaneously, a moving point D starts from point A and moves at a uniform speed of 2 units per second in the direction of $AO$ towards point O. When one point stops moving, the other point will also stop moving. Let the time of movement be $t$ seconds ($t>0$). Directly state the value of $t$ when $\triangle ACD$ is similar to $\triangle AOB$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a plane rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, A is on the positive x-axis, B is on the positive y-axis, and line segment AB is an oblique line in the first quadrant from B downward to the right to A, forming right triangle AOB. Reasoning: The line y=-4/3 x+8 intersects the x-axis at A. Let y=0 to get x=6, so A=(6,0), AO=6; it intersects the y-axis at B. Let x=0 to get y=8, so B=(0,8), BO=8. Therefore AB=sqrt(6^2+8^2)=10. After moving for t seconds, C has moved t units from B along BA, so AC=AB-BC=10-t; D has moved 2t units from A along AO, so AD=2t. D needs 6/2=3 seconds to reach O, and if one side stops the other side also stops, so the valid time is 0<t<=3. Because AC is on AB and AD is on AO, ∠CAD and ∠BAO are the same included angle. By SAS similarity and taking the correspondence A↔A, C↔B, D↔O, there is AC/AB=AD/AO, that is, (10-t)/10=2t/6. Solving gives 6(10-t)=20t, 60-6t=20t, 26t=60, so t=30/13. The other exchanged correspondence would give (10-t)/6=2t/10, t=50/11, which is greater than 3 and does not satisfy the valid motion time.
